title: Going Green Without Going Broke: Tips, Techniques, and Inspiration for Saving Energy, Money, and the Planet
author: Anna M. Clark
target_audience: Homeowners and renters interested in sustainability
Individuals and families seeking to lower their utility bills
People looking for practical, budget-friendly green solutions
Students and educators in environmental studies
core_themes: Incremental lifestyle changes for environmental impact
primary_purpose: To empower readers to adopt environmentally friendly practices in their daily lives without incurring excessive costs, demonstrating that sustainable living is accessible, practical, and can be economical.

structure_format.narrative_style: Practical, encouraging, and informative with a conversational approach
structure_format.organization: Organized into chapters focusing on major aspects of everyday life (energy, water, transportation, food, consumption), each offering actionable advice and real-life examples
features: Personal stories from individuals and communities
Tips categorized by cost and effort levels

key_concepts_lessons: Going green can save you money when approached strategically.
Small changes in daily habits compound to make a significant impact on both finances and the environment.
Evaluating household energy and water use identifies easy areas for eco-friendly improvement.
Sustainable choices, such as efficient appliances and local foods, need not require major lifestyle sacrifices.
Environmental action can start at any budget—many steps are free or low-cost.
Education and long-term mindset shifts are crucial for maintaining sustainable changes.
notable_features: Focuses specifically on green actions that are also budget-friendly
Emphasizes flexibility—readers can choose actions that fit their situation
cultural_historical_context: Published during the late 2000s, in a period marked by rising environmental awareness amid an economic downturn, the book addresses the misconception that living sustainably is expensive and embraces the growing green consumer movement.
reception_impact: Well-received in sustainability circles and by eco-conscious readers
Praised for its practical and approachable advice
Cited as a useful resource for those beginning to transition to a greener lifestyle
Lauded for its focus on achievable change rather than perfectionism
comparable_titles: The Green Book: The Everyday Guide to Saving the Planet One Simple Step at a Time by Elizabeth Rogers and Thomas M. Kostigen
Gorgeously Green: 8 Simple Steps to an Earth-Friendly Life by Sophie Uliano
Zero Waste Home: The Ultimate Guide to Simplifying Your Life by Reducing Your Waste by Bea Johnson
